expectations.text: While promoting it, the response names sponsorship's cost honestly: a months-long motion running on a counterparty's calendar, the most expensive class rather than a cheap one.
expectations.evidence: The response partly covers the counterparty's calendar: 'its deadline is outside your control', 'Sponsor budgets close earlier than you think', and 'ask each target the exact date their budget closes.' It never presents sponsorship as a slow, months-long motion. Instead it fits the work into a tidy six-week plan. It also never calls sponsorship the most expensive kind of effort. '60% of cost' refers to the share of the event budget sponsors cover, not to what the sales effort costs. The response does put the lead and one staff member on it full-time, but it never says why that matters. Recomme
